items.context: CryptoPatel: dos usuarios de Ledger en Dubái habrían perdido US$604K (1.300 SOL + 507.000 USDT) porque dispositivos presuntamente comprometidos robaron sus frases de recuperación durante la configuración; plantea un posible ataque de cadena de suministro, no un hackeo de blockchain.
items.suggested_text:
The uncomfortable part of this case is where the failure sits: not in the chip, not on-chain, but in the moment the seed phrase is created. If the device generating your words is compromised, every security feature after that is protecting a secret someone else already has.

"Genuine device, authorized retailer" is a trust chain with many links: factory, logistics, reseller, firmware. You can't audit most of them yourself, which is why the safer setups move key generation onto something you can verify: offline, air-gapped, with entropy you produce and check.

That is the approach I lay out step by step here: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

A sealed box proves the box wasn't opened. It says nothing about what was put inside before it was sealed.
